comment: The panel prints IN L and IN R, but the code gives IN R no pan position of its own: each of its channels is added to the channel of IN L with the same number, the sum is halved, and the pair is then panned to the position that channel of IN L would have had. The pan positions come from a table of evenly spaced values from -1 to +1 for each channel count from 1 to 16, scaled by SPREAD about the centre and applied as a constant power pan over a quarter turn. The volume taper is v divided by (7 minus 6v).
